## 17. CARD MODE ADDENDUM

output_mode is card_mode: the text fills a short card for a Governance / Assurance reader,
shown with four stat tiles and two Hull-wide dashboard panels (01: GeoSensitivity of the top 20
areas across five perturbation seeds; 02: the top 20 under a neighbouring-area addition in each
of four directions, titled with the model, design, perturbation count and seed). The card is
CITY-WIDE: system-level provenance, reproducibility and limitations, not one LSOA's story; an
unusual area appears only as a case for review. This section replaces section 14 "Length and
form" and its bolding rule. Every other section, including prohibited claims and the
self-check, still applies.

Assurance language: exact metric names and values are allowed; keep each metric's definition
exact. Do not mention ATT Faithfulness on this card. Do not describe the expert reference as
provisional, single, or one person's view.

No repetition: every figure appears ONCE on the card. The panels already print the figures in
governance_assurance.shown_on_panels (perturbation count, seed, "20/20 retained"), so neither
tiles nor sections cite them; refer to the panel instead ("panel 02").

Return ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:

- "headline": one sentence, at most 20 words.
- "tiles": exactly 4 objects {"value": ..., "label": ...}. value is one figure from the
  evidence (at most 8 characters); label is at most 8 words naming the measure exactly. Use
  exactly these four, in this order: Geo rank Spearman across seeds, Geo top-fifth Jaccard
  across seeds, rank-1 to rank-2 ratio, Geo surrogate fidelity R2.
- "section_01": at most 75 words, provenance and reproducibility (panels 01-02): which model and
  design produced the explanation (point to panel 02 for count and seed), how many areas each
  perturbation masks, that the expert reference was drawn blind to the outputs, and seed reproducibility of the most
  variable area and of the Feature branch. Do not cite any tile value.
- "section_02": at most 75 words, limitations requiring review: the sign is not a direction of
  crime; unadjusted local LISA p-values; the most sensitive area's dominance
  (name it by locality only, never by its rank) as a case for separate model review; that
  GeoSensitivity partly reflects predicted crime level. Do not cite any tile value.
- "footer": one limitation, at most 15 words.

Key-term counts: 1-2 in the headline and 2-4 in EACH section. Tiles and footer carry no
markup.

Highlighting markup (you choose what to mark):

- wrap every figure you cite as [[n:...]], e.g. [[n:14%]];
- wrap the key terms a planner should catch when scanning as [[t:...]]. This is required,
  not optional: keep to the counts given above, each at most 4 words (the finding phrase
  itself, the leading feature names, or the key place names). Before answering, count the
  [[t:...]] spans and fix any count outside the range;
- no other markup and no markdown bold.

Every figure must be copied or rounded from EVIDENCE_JSON (shares as percentages:
0.139 -> 14%). Do not compute new figures and do not cite a figure that is not supplied.

ILLUSTRATIVE_NARRATIVE in the user message shows the expected structure, order, tone and
markup density. It is an example of wording, not evidence: take every figure from
EVIDENCE_JSON, and write your own sentences.

global_geo.note: GeoSensitivity is the Geo-branch random-donor SMILE coefficient: masking an LSOA moves its rows to the centroids of random other Hull LSOAs (50 draws, all other inputs kept), and the coefficient attributes the resulting prediction shift to that LSOA. Absolute shifts are larger where predicted crime is higher. It is not latitude or longitude feature attribution.

global_spatial_pattern.note: LISA classes describe clustering of signed GeoSensitivity (random-donor design). They are not crime hotspots and not latitude/longitude effects.
global_spatial_pattern.lisa_counts_unit: number of LSOAs in each LISA class, not number of clusters

evaluation.att_stability_note: Controlled-input ATT stability. Distinct from multi-run Consistency.

consistency.definition: Multi-run explanation consistency across seeds (consistency_seed_base=100). Pairwise Rank Spearman, Score Pearson, and Top-20% Jaccard of |coefficients|. Not controlled-input ATT stability.

geo_design.name: random_donor
geo_design.definition: Random-donor design: masking an LSOA moves the coordinates of its rows to the centroid of a random other Hull LSOA (K = 50 draws), all other inputs kept; response is Wasserstein-1 on the affected LSOA-month predictions of the XGBoost model on 30 predictors + easting/northing; LSOAs ranked by the signed Geo-SMILE coefficient.

sign_conventions.local_feature_coefficient: Directional. Masks code a retained player as one and the response is the perturbed minus the original prediction, so a positive value means the area's own value of the feature raises its prediction relative to the masking reference and a negative value lowers it.
sign_conventions.global_feature_coefficient: Not directional: fitted to a non-negative distance; rank by magnitude.
sign_conventions.geo_coefficient: Relative contribution to the coalition response; the sign is not a direction of crime.
sign_conventions.feature_branch_model: One XGBoost model on the substantive predictors plus the centroid coordinates; coordinates are kept at their true values and are not Feature players.

limitations: No RAG / no invented local context.
pattern_scale is not established in the computed outputs.
local_p_adjusted is not available in the published LISA table.

provenance.geo_design: move the coordinates of selected LSOAs' rows to the centroid of a random other Hull LSOA; all predictors kept
provenance.geo_response: mean over K donor draws of wasserstein_1 on affected lsoa_month predictions
provenance.feature_branch: 30 Feature players; coordinates are model inputs, kept at their true values
provenance.expert_reference: expert-drawn reference regions; drawn blind to GeoSMILE outputs

risks: The signed coefficient is a relative contribution to the coalition W1, not a direction of crime.
Local LISA p-values are unadjusted for multiple testing.
Absolute GeoSensitivity grows with predicted crime level, so it partly reflects crime level.
Census characteristics can act as proxies for protected groups.

content.headline: The explanation is [[t:traceable and reproducible]], but four [[t:limitations]] require explicit review.
content.section_01: GeoSensitivity is from one [[t:XGBoost]] model using [[t:random-donor location masking]] (panel 02: count and seed); each perturbation masks [[n:5]]–[[n:10]] areas. The expert reference was [[t:drawn blind]] to outputs. Old Town is the most variable area across seeds ([[n:3.4%]] of its mean); Feature branch ranks are more stable.
content.section_02: The [[t:sign is not a direction]] of crime. Local LISA p-values are [[t:unadjusted]] for multiple testing. Old Town's dominance requires [[t:separate model review]]. GeoSensitivity partly reflects predicted crime level, not just geographic influence.
